summary: A cardholder starts a cycle with no previous balance, makes a purchase that stays within the credit limit, receives a statement, and then pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario exercises on-time satisfaction of the minimum-payment obligation and the purchase grace-period narrative, with no late fee and no over-limit outcome.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of the billing cycle, so the purchase grace period applies under clause.cost_of_credit_grace_period.
The cardholder's credit limit is $1000.00, and the single purchase in this scenario does not exceed that limit.
The statement closing date is more than 25 days before the due date, satisfying the contract's minimum grace-period timing for purchases.
The payment is made through an approved standard payment method and is credited on the date received.
No cash advances, balance transfers, returned payments, disputed charges, foreign transactions, or other fee-triggering events occur in this scenario.
Because the archetype is on-time full payment, the issuer does not assess any late payment fee or over-limit fee.
